_readme: Misrepresentation Act 1967 (2020 Rev Ed), Singapore. PHASE 1 OUTPUT, all unverified_draft.
Note on authority_basis. The bare text of s.3 catches a term excluding liability or a
remedy for a pre-contractual misrepresentation. It does NOT say on its face that a
non-reliance or entire-agreement clause is such a term — that is judicial gloss. The
s.3 chunk is therefore split in two: the statute-text chunk quotes the section, and the
non-reliance application is a separate case_law_gloss chunk which must name the case it
rests on. That case citation is a KNOWN GAP: no case name has been invented for it.

chunks.exact_wording: If a contract contains a term which would exclude or restrict — (a) any liability to which a party to a contract may be subject by reason of any misrepresentation made by him before the contract was made; or (b) any remedy available to another party to the contract by reason of such a misrepresentation, that term shall be of no effect except in so far as it satisfies the requirement of reasonableness as stated in section 11(1) of the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977, and it is for those claiming that the term satisfies that requirement to show that it does.
chunks.summary: A term excluding liability or a remedy for pre-contractual misrepresentation has no effect unless it is reasonable, and the party relying on it must prove that it is.
applicability_conditions: the contract contains a term that would exclude or restrict liability for, or a remedy in respect of, a misrepresentation made BEFORE the contract was made
AND the term is directed at pre-contractual statements — a clause limiting liability for breach of the contract's own obligations is not within s.3
chunks.note: STITCHED from four rows on the retrieved page: the lead-in ('3. If a contract contains a term which would exclude or restrict —') appeared AFTER paragraphs (a) and (b) and the closing text in the page's table order. The reassembly is confident on content but must be checked for punctuation. Confirmed from source: the section imports section 11(1) of UCTA only — it does not import the Second Schedule.

chunks.provision: Section 3 (as applied to non-reliance and entire agreement clauses)
chunks.exact_wording: If a contract contains a term which would exclude or restrict — (a) any liability to which a party to a contract may be subject by reason of any misrepresentation made by him before the contract was made; or (b) any remedy available to another party to the contract by reason of such a misrepresentation, that term shall be of no effect except in so far as it satisfies the requirement of reasonableness as stated in section 11(1) of the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977, and it is for those claiming that the term satisfies that requirement to show that it does.
chunks.summary: Whether a non-reliance or entire-agreement clause is caught by section 3 turns on judicial interpretation, not on the words of the section. Where it is caught, the clause must satisfy the reasonableness test.
applicability_conditions: the contract contains an entire agreement, non-reliance or acknowledgement-of-no-representation clause
AND the clause is being relied on to defeat a misrepresentation claim rather than merely to define the contractual terms
AND the supporting authority for treating such a clause as within s.3 has been confirmed — this chunk must not fire while supporting_authority is a placeholder
chunks.supporting_authority: UNRESOLVED — case citation required before this chunk may fire (see PHASE2_VERIFICATION.md)

What distinguishes this chunk is authority_basis=case_law_gloss plus a supporting_authority that has NOT been supplied.
